mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 5% over two consecutive quarters signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day forward returns in more than 60% of quarters when FEDFUNDS > 5.0% for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a rise in initial jobless claims (UNRATE) above 6% signals weakening consumer demand and labor market stress, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 20-day forward returns in more than 50% of instances where GDPC1 YoY < -2% and UNRATE > 6%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) above 200,000 for three consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which supports corporate profit margins and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > previous month + 200,000 for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not statistically greater than zero (t-test p > 0.10) during periods of three consecutive months with PAYEMS growth above 200,000.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces revenue for industrial firms and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month - 0.5% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 20-day forward returns in more than 60% of episodes with four consecutive months of INDPRO declines exceeding 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly rise in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above 10% and a decline in Real Personal Income (RSAFS) of more than 1% signals a divergence between housing demand and income growth, which increases default risk and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > previous month + 10% AND RSAFS < previous month - 1%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) when HOUST rises >10% and RSAFS falls >1% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month increase in CPIAUCSL above 0.5% after a period of stable inflation (previous three months < 0.2%) signals a sudden inflation shock, which erodes real purchasing power and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > previous month + 0.5% AND previous three months CPIAUCSL < 0.2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) in months meeting the inflation shock trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% for three consecutive months signals an extremely tight labor market, which increases wage inflation and input costs, ultimately leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as profit margins compress.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of three consecutive months with UNRATE < 3.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annualized decline in Real Personal Consumption Expenditures (GDPC1) of more than 3% for two consecutive quarters, combined with a concurrent decline in Industrial Production (INDPRO) of more than 1% per month for three months, signals a broad-based demand contraction that leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 annualized decline > 3% for two consecutive quarters AND INDPRO < previous month - 1% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during episodes of both GDPC1 annualized decline > 3% for two quarters and INDPRO falling >1% per month for three months.
